prompt:
A voltaic cell is made from a Zn$^{2+}$/Zn half-cell and a Cu$^{2+}$/Cu half-cell under standard conditions.

$E^\ominus(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76\ \text{V}$, $E^\ominus(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\ \text{V}$

**(a)** Calculate the standard cell potential. **[1]**

**(b)** Identify the negative electrode and state the direction of electron flow in the external circuit. **[2]**

**(c)** Calculate $\Delta G^\ominus$ for the cell reaction in kJ mol$^{-1}$. ($F = 96\,500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$) **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}} = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10\ \text{V}$ ✓

**(b)** Zinc is the negative electrode (anode) ✓; electrons flow from zinc to copper through the wire ✓

**(c)** $\Delta G^\ominus = -nFE^\ominus = -2 \times 96\,500 \times 1.10$ ✓ $= -212\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ ✓

prompt:
Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes.

**(a)** Write half-equations for the reactions at the cathode and at the anode. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why sodium is not formed at the cathode. **[1]**

**(c)** State and explain how the anode product would change if the solution were very dilute. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Cathode: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2 + 2\text{OH}^-$ ✓; anode: $2\text{Cl}^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2 + 2e^-$ ✓

**(b)** Water has a much more positive E⦵ than Na⁺/Na, so water is reduced in preference ✓

**(c)** Oxygen (mixed with less chlorine) ✓; at low [Cl⁻] water is oxidised in preference because its E⦵ is lower / concentration favours chloride only when high ✓
